text: Legs: examine the sole, hoof, and joints to identify the cause of lameness. Udder: if a calf isn't suckling, has diarrhea, or isn't growing well, check the udder — first for teats that are too large or malformed, then whether the udder is hard and whether milk expels normally, to diagnose mastitis. Bull penis and testicles: penis length should be enough to reach almost between the front legs during full erection — a bull with too short a penis cannot breed successfully; testicles should move freely within the scrotum and be symmetric. Rectal examination: useful to confirm pregnancy up to about 4 months (the uterus becomes too heavy and drops into the abdomen after that) and, with training, can detect ovarian cysts.
